conviction_note: No primary-document number decides this print. The evidence is: a probable GAAP headline hit from Century merger costs that the Q3 expense guide explicitly left out (negative, a one-off); a Fed hike on 2026-09-16 that this self-described asset-sensitive bank should turn into a firmer Q4 NIM outlook (positive, guidance); and a Century deal that closes about 2026-11-01 with 25%+ EPS accretion already published (largely priced). These roughly offset. The bar is disputed (EW $1.00, EW-derived summary $1.05, TickFlow $1.08), so every size is capped small. p_up 53 rests on the name's beat record (6 of the last 7) and the rate tailwind, against a stock already up about 8% since the last print. abs_move 2.6 is the 2.4% median reaction nudged up because this call is the first with pro forma Century commentary after a rate hike.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS. Sources disagree: Earnings Whispers consensus $1.00 with a whisper of $1.06 and revenue (NII) of $23.73M (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/BSVN, read 2026-10-14). A search summary quoting Earnings Whispers gives $1.05, and TickFlow gives $1.08 from 2 analysts (https://www.tickflow.io/stock/BSVN/forecast; returned HTTP 429 on fetch, snippet only). MarketBeat lists no Q3 consensus (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BSVN/earnings/). Company guidance: Q3 noninterest expense $9.5-9.7M excluding M&A transaction costs, core NIM 4.45-4.53% excluding loan fees and excess liquidity, and full-year loan growth in the mid-single digits (Q2 call, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). With no two estimate sources agreeing, the bar is disputed and every finding that depends on it is capped. print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of GAAP EPS against a ~$1.03 midpoint, assuming merger costs land in Q3. On a core basis I estimate roughly +2 to +4%.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 148K shares, ~1.6% of float, 2.6 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/BSVN, settlement date not stated, short-volume data dated 2026-10-13). Not crowded. An older Benzinga page showed 54K shares and 4.5 days. There is no options market (baseline options.status = no_options_market), so there is no skew. The tape: spot $55.02, 4.2% below the 52-week high, 20-day run-up +1.2%, 5-day -0.2%, 20-day realised vol 13.2%, and +8.2% post-earnings drift since the 2026-07-16 release (Earnings Whispers). The average analyst target is $57.33 from 3 Buy ratings (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/BSVN). Piper Sandler's target is $61 (2026-07-17) and KBW's $56 (https://www.investing.com/equities/bank7).

findings.finding: Bank7 won the court auction for 71% of Century Financial on 2026-09-03 with a $91.0M bid ($88.96M net of a $2.04M break-up credit, up from the $68M stalking-horse price). It then signed a full merger agreement on 2026-09-16 ($70M cash + 1,232,657 BSVN shares, ~$137.3M). The Q2 call set the Q3 noninterest expense guide at $9.5-9.7M and said 'M&A transaction expenses are more difficult to estimate', i.e. outside the guide. Q3 GAAP EPS is therefore likely to carry auction, legal and advisory costs that a $1.00-1.08 consensus may not include. Each ~$1M pre-tax is ~$0.08 of EPS on ~9.6M diluted shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was a GAAP headline miss ($0.87 vs $1.03-1.04) driven by a one-off energy-asset loss and M&A/IT costs, with core EPS cited at ~$1.06. The stock moved -2.51% on the release (baseline) and has since drifted up ~8%, so holders looked through the one-off within weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus for this two-to-three-analyst name has not visibly moved since the deal. Earnings Whispers still shows a $1.00 consensus and a $1.06 whisper, above the Q2 GAAP print. If merger costs were modelled in, the estimates would sit below the ~$1.05-1.10 core run-rate the guide implies. They do not.
findings.independence: The Q2 call transcript gives the expense guide and its exclusion of M&A transaction costs (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). The 2026-09-17 merger 8-K and investor deck say deal metrics 'include transaction-related expenses' but give no amount (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036855/ef20081983_ex99-2.htm). Both are company documents. No independent quantification exists.

findings.finding: On a core basis, the company's own Q3 guide implies EPS at or slightly above the bar. Core NIM is guided to 4.45-4.53% on ~$1.83B of earning assets, so ~$20.5-20.9M of core NII, plus loan fees from the 'significant paydowns' expected in H2. Q2 reported NIM was 4.81% including fees, and NII was $21.91M. Noninterest income is ~$1.0M with oil and gas revenue now gone (the properties were sold 2026-04-10). Expenses are guided at $9.5-9.7M against ~$9.9M in Q2 excluding the $2.0M of oil-and-gas expense. Provision has been zero for two quarters, on a $19.5M ACL. That arithmetic gives roughly $1.05-1.10 of core EPS against a $1.00-1.08 bar. The result sits inside what management guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Clean beats of +$0.09 to +$0.24 bought +0.57% (Q3 2025), +1.34% (Q4 2025), +1.89% (Q2 2025) and +2.4% (Q1 2026). Beats in Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 still fell 3.2% and 4.8% in weak tapes (baseline). The name beat 6 of its last 7 quarters (MarketBeat).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The arithmetic follows the company's published guide, and the stock trades near its 52-week high. It is filed because the bar is split between $1.00 and $1.08, so whether the core number reads as a beat depends on which bar the tape uses.
findings.independence: The guide figures come from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) and the oil-and-gas exit from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746129/000114036126032024/bsvn-20260630.htm). The beat history comes from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BSVN/earnings/). All are company-derived.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first move since holding at 3.50-3.75% from Dec 2025. On the Q2 call Bank7 called itself asset-sensitive and said a hike would benefit it, while setting a 'static' June core NIM of 4.51% as the Q3 baseline. Q3 itself gets only ~2 weeks of the hike. The Q4 NIM and NII outlook given on this call should be firmer than the static baseline the market was handed in July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior hike cycle is in the baseline window. The Q1 2026 print, the strongest beat (+$0.24) with reported NIM above core on fees, bought +2.4%, the largest positive reaction in the last seven.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The hike is public and sector-wide. What is not public is Bank7's quantified Q4 NIM guide after it: the July guide was set before the hike and estimates have not visibly moved (Earnings Whispers consensus is still $1.00). Deposit costs of 2.28-2.30% could reprice up and offset part of the asset benefit. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The company's asset-sensitivity statement on the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) is a different source from the Fed release. The link from macro to company is confirmed only qualitatively by the company.

findings.finding: The Century merger is on an accelerated path. Century shareholders approved it on 2026-10-09; Federal Reserve and New Mexico FID approvals or non-objections have been received; closing is expected about 2026-11-01, a month inside the 2026-11-30 termination date (8-K of 2026-10-09). The deal deck gives 25%+ EPS accretion, ~11% TBV dilution, a 1.7-year earnback, pro forma CET1 of 10.0% and TCE/TA of 8.3%, a $3.3B pro forma balance sheet, and a price of 6.3x 2027E earnings plus synergies. This call is the first earnings call since the merger agreement and will carry pro forma commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior earnings call has carried an acquisition this size (the deal ~doubles assets from $1.9B). The stock is +8.2% since 2026-07-16 through the auction win and merger announcement, so the deal has been bought, not sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The deal metrics are public and the stock is near its high. The 5-day run-up of -0.2% shows no reaction to the 2026-10-09 approval 8-K. The unpriced part is any confirmation or change of the accretion number, cost saves (the deck gives no dollar figure) and Century's actual earnings, which are not disclosed anywhere.
findings.independence: The investor deck has the metrics (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036855/ef20081983_ex99-2.htm). It shares the company as the source. Piper's Nathan Race called Century's deposits low-cost and high-quality (https://www.americanbanker.com/news/bank7-targets-sept-3-close-for-contested-n-m-rival-buyout).

findings.finding: The balance sheet was flat to shrinking in H1. Gross loans went from $1,609.4M at 2025-12-31 to $1,600.1M at 2026-06-30, with agricultural loans -$16.9M and C&I -$24.1M. Deposits fell $63.0M to $1,637.8M. Yet the full-year guide is mid-single-digit loan growth, with 'significant paydowns' in H2 and Q3 fundings expected at roughly double Q2. Hitting the guide needs ~10% annualized H2 growth, so Q3 period-end loans are a visible test. Paydowns also lift loan-fee income, which offsets part of the hit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed flat loans YTD alongside the headline miss: -2.51%. The line's separate effect is not isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: The 10-Q loan table is barely read on a two-to-three-analyst name. If the market doubted the growth guide, estimates would have fallen after Q2. They did not.
findings.independence: The guide language comes from the call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Both are company documents, so this is one fact pattern, not two.

findings.finding: A third-party (AI-generated) read of the Q2 10-Q reports 8 material weaknesses in ICFR at 2026-06-30, in IT controls, segregation of duties and disclosures. On the Q2 call, management said remediation would be largely complete by end of Q3. Any slippage in the Q3 release or 10-Q is a quality-of-earnings flag, and the remediation consulting cost sits in the expense line.
findings.why_not_priced: The weakness count was not in the wire copy of the Q2 release. I could not read Item 4 of the 10-Q to verify the count (the fetched text ended at Note 5), so the finding is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q2 call mentions material-weakness IT remediation expected largely complete by end of Q3 (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). That confirms a weakness exists, not the count.

outside_window.finding: The 1,232,657 BSVN shares issued to Century holders at close (~13% of the ~9.6M current share count) are restricted. Bank7 agreed to file a resale registration statement after closing, which creates a later supply overhang once the shares become saleable.
The Century merger closes about 2026-11-01 and moves combined assets from $1.9B to ~$3.3B, with 25%+ EPS accretion claimed. The accretion is realised only from Q4 2026 onward.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The evidence is balanced: a modest positive lean from the rate hike and the beat record against a likely GAAP headline hit from merger costs and a stock already up ~8% since the last print. Nothing cuts hard against the near-flat 20-day run-up.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar: EW $1.00 vs $1.05/$1.08, MarketBeat none) plus rule 2 (merger costs are a one-off with no path to the guide): the merger-cost headline finding goes from -0.6 to -0.4.
Rule 5 (unverified third-party proxy): the material-weakness finding, whose count I could not verify in the 10-Q, goes from -0.2 to -0.15.
Rule 5 (macro transmission): the Fed-hike guidance finding is left at +0.6, because the company itself confirmed asset sensitivity on the call.
Rules 1, 7 and 8 changed nothing: no skew, the short is not crowded, and no confirmed unpriced company-level number exists to size up. p_up and abs_move_pct are unchanged.
